# *The Rescue*: report

A 20-second original animation. Two characters, MILO and JUNO, work in a workshop.

1. MILO tries to move a heavy container and loses control of it.
2. A falling support pins him.
3. JUNO runs to help. She cannot lift the post by hand, so she uses a pry bar as a lever to free him.
4. She helps him up, and they share a fist bump.

There is no dialogue.

**This report claims no quality score.** Technical checks pass, but artistic quality needs a human review (`docs/REVIEW_RUBRIC.md`). The film was **authored by hand** (`examples/build_rescue.py`), not generated by the AI Director. Section 5 explains why.

## 2. What happens, and what causes it

The times come from the simulation.

| Time | Beat | Cause (simulated) |
|---|---|---|
| 0–1.5 | Both walk in. A ratchet strap ties the container to a tall, top-heavy support post | — |
| 1.8 | MILO braces and pushes | `push` applies a bounded force: 1.25 × his strength of 52,000 = 65,000 |
| 3.5 | It breaks loose and outruns him. He stumbles and falls prone | Static friction of 60,540 is exceeded. Sliding friction is far lower (stick-slip), so the container accelerates faster than he can follow and contact is lost (`push_lost`) |
| 3.6–3.7 | The strap snaps taut, yanks the post over and breaks | The rope reaches its length (`rope_taut`). Its tension passes the 900,000 breaking force (`rope_snap`). The post's centre of mass is high, so the yank topples it |
| 4.9 | The post lands across MILO's legs | `pinned`: a vertical contact impulse between the post and his lying body |
| 5.4 | JUNO, at the bench, reacts and runs to him | `wait_for event:pinned@milo`, then `notice`, then `run_to char:milo` |
| 6.8–8.2 | She tries to lift the post's end by hand and fails | `lift` regulates her force toward a 30-unit rise, clamped to her strength (45,000). The post rises 5.4 units (`lift_fail`). A test raises her strength to 160,000 and she *does* lift it, so physics decides, not the script |
| 9.2–12.8 | She spots the pry bar on the rack, runs for it and carries it back | `use_lever`: run, pick up, carry, place. The bar is pinned at the toolbox top, with its tip under the post's end |
| 12.8 | She bears down on the handle | The handle force is regulated and clamped to her strength. Leverage lifts the post's end (`load_off`) |
| 13.7–15.3 | MILO crawls out and clears the post (`freed`) | `crawl_out` waits for `load_off`, then keeps going until he has a margin for getting up |
| 15.9 | She lets the post drop and offers her hand | `use_lever` holds until `get_up_start@milo`, then `offer_hand` |
| 17.6–18.5 | He takes her hand and is pulled to his feet | `get_up` with a helper. Both hands IK to one shared contact point (`hand_grab`, `stood_up`) |
| 19.0 | Fist bump | `gesture fist_bump`: both fists meet at a shared point |

The score follows the same events: calm, then tension from `push_lost`, release at `freed`, and resolution at `stood_up`. The sound effects are bound to the events: strain, scrape, the strap snapping, impacts, lever creak, tap.

## 3. What already existed and what had to be built

### Reused unchanged

- the rig, forward and inverse kinematics, the locomotion gait, `walk_to`, `run_to`, `turn`, `notice`, `look_at`;
- the motion-library and blending infrastructure;
- the camera director: modes, `include`, composition guards;
- the Skia renderer and its themes;
- the sound director, recorded samples, panning and reverb;
- the event system and shot exit conditions;
- the QA inspector and review artefacts;
- the PhysicsWorld wrapper around pymunk.

### New, general (not specific to this scene)

| Capability | Files |
|---|---|
| Props with kind, angle, stick-slip friction, centre of mass, non-solid set dressing, depth (`z`), and whether characters collide with them | `scene/schema.py`, `physics/world.py`, `scene/runtime.py` |
| Ropes and straps that go taut and snap at a breaking force | `physics/world.py` (`add_rope`, `rope_tension`, `cut_rope`), `scene/runtime.py` |
| Friction changes reach live contacts (Chipmunk caches friction per contact) | `physics/world.py` (`set_friction`) |
| Bodies pass props while standing and become solid when lying (collision categories) | `physics/world.py` |
| Bounded-force actions: `push`, `lift`, `use_lever` (pick up, carry, place, press, hold, release) | `motion/interaction.py` |
| Knock-down to prone; pinning detected from contact impulses; `struggle`, `crawl_out`, `get_up` (alone or helped) | `motion/interaction.py`, `motion/interaction_anim.py` |
| Two-character contact: `offer_hand` and `get_up` meet at a shared point; `gesture` (fist bump, shoulder pat, wave); `wait_for` events; `char:` and `prop:` targets for walking, looking and camera `include` | `motion/interaction.py`, `motion/interaction_anim.py`, `render/pipeline.py`, `camera/director.py` |
| Lying-body poses: prone, crawl, push-up, kneel, stand. Floor-safe elbow bend, knee clearance and toe clamps | `motion/interaction_anim.py`, `rig/stickman.py` (`arm_ik(bend=…)`) |
| Renderer: extruded container, post (cap plate, hazard bands), pry bar, toolbox, strap (sag, taut, snapped ends); props depth-sorted; a load drawn over the body it pins; lying bodies drawn in front | `render/skia_renderer.py` |
| Sounds: strain, strap snap, lever creak, tap; score keyed to danger and release | `audio/sound_director.py` |
| Diagnostics tool | `scripts/interaction_diagnostics.py` |
| AI Director: prompt generated from the schema, sound-name validation, posture rules, simulation feedback with physics numbers, logs preserved | `ai/director.py`, `cli.py` (`apex plan --log-dir`) |

### Scene-specific (data only)

Positions, masses, frictions, strap slack, the two action lists, the colours, and the shot list in `examples/build_rescue.py`. Tuning them took several sweeps, for example the strap slack and friction against the container's final position.

### Problems found along the way and fixed in general code

- Friction changes were ignored by live contacts.
- A standing character's body shoved props aside.
- A prop parked in a path blocked the container (scene layout).
- Elbows flipped through the floor when the body was rotated.
- A knee-clearance pass lifted a flat body by 40 units.
- Legs rotated into the floor during the push-up.
- A side bump counted as "pinned".
- Getting up moved the hips back under the load.

## 5. AI Director: an honest account

The brief asked for a real natural-language-to-animation test through OpenRouter. The same story text (`docs/ai_runs/rescue_story.txt`) was planned by the real model each time, with every raw response preserved.

| Run | Engine state | Model | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rescue_baseline` | Before any change | claude-sonnet-5.5 | **Accepted, but fake.** The push, the trap and the lift were `idle` with text notes; the lever was a gravity switch; the sound names didn't exist. The render failed QA (5 failures) |
| `rescue_upgraded_v1` | New actions; prompt from the schema | claude-sonnet-5.5 | **Accepted, but did not play out.** It used the real actions, but its container (260 mass, static friction 0.9) could never break loose and it had no strap. In the render nothing falls and 15 QA checks fail. This exposed the posture bug (struggling while standing), since fixed |
| `rescue_upgraded_v2` | Plus a dry-run check for unfinished steps | claude-sonnet-5.5 | **Failed** after 5 attempts. The feedback loop worked (schema, then posture, then simulation feedback), but the last attempt used an unknown sound |
| `rescue_upgraded_v3` | Plus physics numbers in the feedback | claude-sonnet-5.5 | **Crashed** on attempt 5: an empty model response. Handled since, and the output budget was raised after truncated JSON |
| `rescue_upgraded_v4` | Plus robust parsing, 8 attempts | claude-sonnet-5.5 | **Failed, but close.** On attempt 6 the simulation played push, break loose, strap snap and fall, but the post missed the fallen character, so nothing was pinned |
| `rescue_upgraded_v5_opus` | Plus rope-field aliases | claude-opus-5.5 | **Failed, closest.** On attempt 6 the simulation played push, break loose, strap snap, fall, **pinned** and the lift attempt. The plan then broke on a race: it started `crawl_out` before the post had landed, so the character crawled while it fell, and the helped `get_up` waited for a hand that never came. The last attempts went to field-name slips (`a_anchor`, `a_point`) |

**Conclusion.** The natural-language workflow is real and connected, and its feedback loop measurably moved the plans toward a working physical setup. It did **not** produce an accepted plan that plays the whole story within the attempts allowed. The delivered film is **manually scripted**, using the same engine features the AI can call. The AI's best plans and their failures are preserved and explained.

Total OpenRouter cost of all the runs: about $3.36.

**Engine findings from the AI runs:**

- `crawl_out` should wait while a load is still falling toward the character, rather than starting at once if nothing is on them yet. That would have saved the Opus plan.
- Rope fields need tolerant naming. Two aliases were added; the models also tried others.
- The planner needs the trapping geometry as an *intent*, not as numbers.

The missing piece is the tuning that took sweeps by hand (strap slack against the container's travel, post placement against where the person falls). A planner needs either many more simulate-and-adjust iterations or a higher-level "trap" intent that the engine solves itself. See section 7.

## 6. Remaining limitations and visual-quality defects

| # | Defect / limitation | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | The post rebounds (its base end kicks up to about 150) when its heavy cap end lands across MILO's legs. Plausible for a rigid post on a rigid body, probably livelier than reality: lying bodies are kinematic, with no compliance | Medium |
| R2 | During the hand-lift attempt JUNO stands over MILO's body (both on the same depth plane), which crowds the frame | Medium |
| R3 | The toolbox (fulcrum) sits beside MILO's head while he is pinned and crowds his face, though it is drawn behind him | Low |
| R4 | The fist bump reads more as hands meeting than a crisp bump: no anticipation or recoil keys yet | Low |
| R5 | No facial acting. Pain, fear and relief are carried by posture and timing alone | Medium |
| R6 | The fall to prone is a scripted pose curve driven by the physics event (`push_lost`). The body itself is not a ragdoll | Medium (architectural) |
| R7 | Characters share one depth plane: they cannot pass *beside* each other in depth, only overlap in 2D | Medium (architectural) |
| R8 | The screen-direction flip at the final cut (QA warning) | Low |
| R9 | The physical setup needs hand tuning (layout sweeps). The AI Director cannot yet do it reliably (section 5) | High for automation |

## 7. Next steps toward the reference films (in the agreed order)

1. **Combat and acrobatics** on top of this contact layer: strikes with hit reactions, blocks, knockbacks, and an active ragdoll fall that replaces R6.
2. **Music-beat sync** for actions and cuts.
3. **Breakable objects** and larger particle effects.
4. **A 3D renderer backend**, only if fly-throughs are wanted (the adapter is in place).

Engine work that would also help the AI Director:

- A per-character depth lane (fixes R2, R3, R7).
- Compliant lying bodies (fixes R1).
- A small layout solver for intents like "this prop should fall on that character", so planners state the intent and the engine finds the numbers (fixes R9).
